text: In the land where no wise men are, men of little wit are lords; And the castor-oil's a tree, where no tree else its shade affords.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material

text: That friend only is the true friend who is near when trouble comes; That man only is the brave man who can bear the battle-drums.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material

text: Sentences of studied wisdom, nought avail they unapplied; Though the blind man hold a lantern, yet his footsteps stray aside.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material

text: Mud may be wiped, but wise men plunge not in it.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material

text: Give mean men power, and give thy throat to the knife; The Mouse, made Tiger, sought his master's life.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material

text: While the hungry lion slumbers, not a deer comes to his den.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material

text: A modest manner fits a maid, And Patience is a man's adorning.
era: compiled c. 8th-12th c. CE from older material
